questions.title: In-Degree of a Node
questions.description:
In a directed graph the in-degree of u counts incoming arrows — every occurrence of u inside any neighbour list. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int inDegree(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int u)

It must return the number of directed edges pointing at node u.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed edge u -> v. Last line: the queried node u.

Output Format:
One line with the in-degree of u.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Server Rack Connections
questions.description:
A data-centre wiring map is an undirected graph; the rack with the most cables is the maintenance hotspot, so every rack's connection count matters. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int degree(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int u)

It must return the number of cables attached to rack u (its degree in the undirected graph).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a cable between racks u and v. Last line: the queried rack u.

Output Format:
One line with the number of connections.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Count the Edges
questions.description:
In an adjacency list every directed edge appears exactly once, so the edge count is just the total length of all neighbour lists. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int edgeCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the number of directed edges in the graph (the sum of all adjacency-list sizes).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed edge u -> v (0-indexed).

Output Format:
One line with the edge count.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Degree of a Node
questions.description:
In an undirected adjacency list, the degree of a node is simply how many neighbours are stored against it. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int degree(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int u)

It must return the degree of node u in the undirected graph.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected edge. Last line: the queried node u.

Output Format:
One line with the degree of u.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: BFS Traversal
questions.description:
Breadth-first search explores a graph in rings: the start node, then its neighbours, then their neighbours. Neighbours are processed in the order the adjacency list stores them. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void bfs(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int start, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the BFS visit order (starting with start) into out, using a queue and a visited array so no node is visited twice. The harness prints the order space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected edge. Last line: the start node.

Output Format:
One line with the BFS order space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: DFS Traversal
questions.description:
Depth-first search dives along one neighbour chain as far as possible before backtracking, visiting neighbours in adjacency-list order. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void dfs(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int start, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the recursive DFS visit order (starting with start) into out, marking nodes visited so no node is recorded twice. You may write an additional static helper for the recursion. The harness prints the order space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected edge. Last line: the start node.

Output Format:
One line with the DFS order space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Degree from the Matrix
questions.description:
An adjacency matrix stores a 1 in cell [u][j] whenever u and j are joined; the degree of u is the number of 1s in row u. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int degreeFromMatrix(int[][] m, int u)

It must return the degree of node u by counting the 1s in row u of the (undirected, symmetric) matrix.

Input Format:
Line 1: V. Then V lines, each with V space-separated 0/1 entries — the adjacency matrix. Last line: the queried node u.

Output Format:
One line with the degree of u.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, matrix entries are 0 or 1, 0 <= u < V
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= V <= 50, matrix entries are 0 or 1, 0 <= u < V

questions.title: Rumor Spread Order
questions.description:
A rumor travels through a friendship network ring by ring: first the teller's direct friends, then their friends. Broadcast exactly like BFS, friends in adjacency order. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void bfs(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int start, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the order in which people hear the rumor (starting with start) into out, using a queue and a visited array.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a friendship. Last line: the teller start.

Output Format:
One line with the spread order space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Package Dependency Walk
questions.description:
An installer explores a package's dependency graph depth-first: follow one dependency chain to its end before trying the next dependency, in adjacency order. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void dfs(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int start, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the recursive DFS visit order (starting with start) into out with a visited array. You may write an additional static helper for the recursion.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed dependency u depends on v. Last line: the entry package start.

Output Format:
One line with the walk order space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Campus Road Count
questions.description:
A campus map is an undirected graph; facilities planning needs the number of road segments. Each road appears twice across the adjacency lists — once from each end. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int roadCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the number of undirected roads (the total of all adjacency-list sizes divided by 2).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a road between intersections u and v.

Output Format:
One line with the road count.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Cluster Count
questions.description:
A company network splits into isolated clusters of machines; each cluster is one connected component of the undirected graph. Sweep every node and start one traversal per unvisited cluster. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int countComponents(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the number of connected components in the undirected graph. You may write additional static helper methods if you need them.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected link.

Output Format:
One line with the number of clusters.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Flight Reachability
questions.description:
An airline's route map is a directed graph; a booking desk must say whether destination t can be reached from origin s at all. Dive depth-first from s and see if t ever turns up. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static boolean reachable(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s, int t)

It must return true when t is reachable from s following directed edges, false otherwise. A node reaches itself.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed flight u -> v. Last line: "s t".

Output Format:
One line with true or false.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, t, u, v < V

questions.title: Fewest Metro Stops
questions.description:
Metro lines form an undirected graph; journey planning means the FEWEST stops between two stations — exactly what BFS distance measures. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int hopDistance(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s, int t)

It must return the minimum number of edges on any path from s to t, or -1 when t is unreachable. A station is 0 stops from itself.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a track between stations. Last line: "s t".

Output Format:
One line with the fewest stops or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, t, u, v < V

questions.title: Fan-Out Report
questions.description:
In a notification graph each server forwards alerts to the servers on its adjacency list; operations wants every server's fan-out (out-degree) in one report. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] outDegrees(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return an array where res[u] is the out-degree of node u (the size of its adjacency list).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed forwarding rule u -> v.

Output Format:
One line with V numbers space-separated — the out-degrees of nodes 0 .. V-1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Pipeline Total Length
questions.description:
A weighted adjacency matrix stores pipeline lengths between pump stations (0 means no pipeline). The network is undirected, so every length sits symmetrically across the diagonal — total it by reading each cell once, above the diagonal. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int totalWeight(int[][] w)

It must return the sum of w[i][j] over every pair i < j with a nonzero entry (entries above the diagonal already cover every undirected edge exactly once).

Input Format:
Line 1: V. Then V lines, each with V space-separated integers — the symmetric weight matrix (0 = no pipeline, diagonal 0).

Output Format:
One line with the total pipeline length.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= weight <= 1000

questions.title: Two-Way Street Check
questions.description:
A road database claims every street is two-way, but data entry errors slip in. Verify the stored directed adjacency list: for EVERY edge u -> v there must be a matching edge v -> u. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static boolean isUndirected(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return true when every directed edge u -> v has its reverse v -> u in the adjacency list, false otherwise. Self-loops pass (u -> u reverses to itself).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a stored directed edge.

Output Format:
One line with true or false.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Coverage Distance Map
questions.description:
A delivery hub maps how many legs separate it from every other depot: BFS from the hub fills a distance array, -1 where a depot is unreachable. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] bfsDistances(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s)

It must return an array dist where dist[u] is the fewest edges from s to u (0 for s itself) and -1 when u is unreachable from s. Use a queue and process neighbours in adjacency order.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected link. Last line: the hub s.

Output Format:
One line with V numbers space-separated — the distances from s to nodes 0 .. V-1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, u, v < V

questions.title: LAN Topology Check
questions.description:
A valid LAN tree topology must be connected AND hold exactly V - 1 cables — any fewer splits the network, any more creates a redundant loop. Count the cables first, then sweep one traversal from node 0 and confirm every node was reached. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isTree(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return 1 when the undirected graph is a tree (connected with exactly V - 1 edges) and 0 otherwise. You may write additional static helper methods if you need them.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected cable.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Component Size Report
questions.description:
An operations dashboard lists every isolated cluster of the network with its machine count, sorted ascending. Measure each component with one BFS, then sort the sizes. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static ArrayList<Integer> componentSizes(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the sizes of all connected components of the undirected graph, sorted in ascending order (e.g. with Collections.sort). You may write additional static helper methods if you need them.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected link.

Output Format:
One line with the component sizes ascending, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Packet Route Trace
questions.description:
A router reports the exact path a packet takes: BFS from the source while remembering each node's parent, then walk the parent chain back from the destination to rebuild the route. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void hopPath(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s, int t, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the shortest directed path from s to t (both endpoints included, s first) into out, or just -1 when t is unreachable. Use BFS with a parent array; s reaches itself with the single-node path.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed link. Last line: "s t".

Output Format:
One line with the path nodes space-separated, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, t, u, v < V
